value.statement: For a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channel W, let t_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)-I_p(X;Z), let C be the upper concave envelope on the input simplex, and define A_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)+C[-t_W](p), D_W(p)=I_p(X;Z)+C[t_W](p), B_avg(W)=sup_p(A_W(p)+D_W(p))/2, and B_br(W)=sup_p min{A_W(p),D_W(p)}. Then B_avg is exactly additive under arbitrary finite products of finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channels, including correlated product-channel input laws and envelope auxiliaries joint across factors. On a receiver-skew channel, where an involutive input relabeling exchanges the receiver marginals up to output relabeling, B_br(W)=B_avg(W); finite products preserve this equality and additivity. Consequently, for the half-skew BSSC P and every finite integer n≥1, B_br(P^{×n})=B_avg(P^{×n})=n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) bits. These are two separately relaxed scalar UV functionals; the result does not establish tensorization of the full UV region, optimization over a common joint (U,V), the GK functional, broadcast-channel capacity, or capacity tensorization. The resulting separately relaxed UV value is non-frontier and does not change the governed capacity interval.

value.currentStateSummary: The averaged separately relaxed UV scalar is exactly additive for arbitrary finite-alphabet broadcast-channel products, including correlated product inputs and envelope auxiliaries joint across factors. On receiver-skew channels the branchwise scalar equals the averaged scalar, and finite products preserve that equality and additivity. Thus both scalars on every finite n-fold power of the half-skew BSSC equal n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4). The general theorem and specialization are analytic; the current executable audit checks only selected algebraic and numerical specialization facts. This result concerns only the two separately relaxed scalars, is non-frontier, and does not establish full-UV-region, common joint-(U,V), GK-functional, or capacity tensorization.
